subject: Private hosting tech recap — residency constraints & procurement triggers
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Amrita Singh <amrita.singh@arcadiahealth.com>, Ben Wallace <ben.wallace@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Private hosting tech recap — residency constraints & procurement triggers

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment after the discovery call — focused on the on-prem / VPC requirement you described.

Summary of key pain points / drivers:
- Regulatory: Arcadia’s PHI-processing pipelines must remain within US-controlled networks; some workloads will require strict residency and auditability (state-level and federal compliance).
- Isolation: Production inference must run in a logically (and potentially physically) isolated environment with no public egress except through approved proxies/peering.
- Procurement gating: Procurement requires an MSA/SOW template, SOC2 summary, and published data-retention guarantees before chief procurement signs off.
- Network constraints: limited inbound ports, no direct public IPs for inference hosts, mandatory TLS termination at your edge, and egress restricted to a small IP range that you control.
- Timeline: pilot (sandboxed VPC) targeted within 6 weeks; full production rollout targeted in Q4 (3–4 months), contingent on procurement and security approvals.

Action items we committed to (owners / target dates):
1) Arcadia: share network topology & firewall rules (diagram + existing peering details) — owner: Ben — due: 2027-05-07.
2) Arcadia: confirm which environments must be air-gapped vs. VPC-accessible (list of workloads) — owner: Amrita — due: 2027-05-07.
3) Redwood: provide a concise network requirements doc and suggested peering model + IP ranges — owner: Karthik — deliver: 2027-05-05. [Attachment: redwood_network_requirements_v1.pdf]
4) Redwood: draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with milestones for pilot -> prod, and a procurement checklist (MSA + SOC2 summary) — owner: Marissa & Laura — deliver: 2027-05-06. [Attachment: mutual-action-plan-arcadia.xlsx]
5) All: schedule a focused security & procurement call to review SOC2 artifacts and SSO/KMS expectations — proposed window: 2027-05-10 to 2027-05-12.

Risk & notes:
- If Arcadia requires a fully air-gapped (no network bridge) deployment for certain PHI workloads, our on-prem package and onsite support model will need explicit SOW terms (installation window, remote support rules).
- KMS/HSM integration: we can support customer-managed keys; we’ll need more detail on your KMS provider and HSM attestation needs.

Next steps (short):
- Ben/Amrita: drop topology and list of air-gapped workloads by Friday (2027-05-07).
- I’ll circulate the network requirements PDF and a first-draft MAP by Wednesday (2027-05-05).
- Laura/Marissa will prepare procurement artifacts and a redline window for the MSA.

Attachments (stubs):
- redwood_network_requirements_v1.pdf (PDF, 340 KB)
- mutual-action-plan-arcadia.xlsx (Excel, 28 KB)

If anything above is off or missing, please flag and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll schedule the security/procurement deep-dive once we have the topology and the procurement contact copied.

—
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0124

From: Amrita Singh <amrita.singh@arcadiahealth.com>

Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private hosting tech recap — residency constraints & procurement triggers

Hi Karthik — thanks for the clear write-up. This matches our internal notes. A few clarifications and adds:

1) Procurement: I’m looping in our procurement alias (procurement@arcadiahealth.com) for visibility. They need a redline window for the MSA and a short lead-time estimate for on-prem install (hours on site, number of engineers).

2) Topology: Ben will attach the network diagram (DMZ/proxy, internal VLANs, firewall ACLs). Ben — can you include the current IP blocks and whether the egress will be NATed behind a proxy?

3) Air-gap scope: We expect two workloads to be candidate-airgapped: (a) Claims PHI inference, (b) Clinical notes PII processing. Everything else can live in a locked VPC.

4) SOC2 / security artifacts: procurement wants a SOC2 summary (not full report) and our standard encryption-at-rest/cross-region policy doc. Can you provide a redacted SOC2 and a short FAQ for encryption/KMS?

5) Security call: we prefer 2027-05-11 at 10:00 AM PT or 2027-05-12 at 9:00 AM PT. Please confirm.

Ben — attaching the diagram now (attachment: arcadia_network_v1.vsdx).

Thanks,
Amrita
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Arcadia Health
amrita.singh@arcadiahealth.com | (617) 555-0921
